Q1. Which of the following statements about physical idealizations is most reasonable?
A. Treating a horse as a perfect sphere is appropriate when calculating the bending of its knee joint while running.
Joint-level motion depends on the animal’s shape and internal structure, so a sphere model throws away the key geometry.
B. Treating a horse as a point mass is appropriate when estimating how far it travels across a multi-kilometer field over several minutes.
Over distances far larger than the animal’s size, the center-of-mass position change can be modeled well by a point mass.
C. It is invalid to model a situation as vacuum-like under any circumstances, even if drag forces are negligible.
“Ignoring air resistance” is precisely an idealization that approximates vacuum when drag is small compared with other forces.
D. None of the above is reasonable.
Option B is a standard and defensible approximation for large-scale translational motion.

Q2. Which of the following equations is correct?
A. 1 nickel = 1 $
A nickel is only a small fraction of a dollar, not equal to a full dollar.
B. 1 = 0.05
This drops the units and incorrectly asserts a pure number equality.
C. 1 nickel = 0.05 $
A nickel is defined as five cents, i.e., 0.05 dollars.
D. 20 nickels = 0.05 $
Twenty nickels is 20 × 0.05 = 1.00 dollar, not 0.05 dollars.

Q3. Which option has the incorrect unit?
A. Power: watt (W)
A watt is the correct SI unit of power (J/s).
B. Pressure: newton/meter2 (N/m2)
Pressure is force per area, so N/m2 (pascal) is correct.
C. Electric charge: coulomb/second (C/s)
C/s is the unit of electric current (ampere), while charge alone is measured in coulombs (C).
D. Momentum: kilogram·meter/second (kg·m/s)
Momentum is mass times velocity, giving SI units of kg·m/s.

Q7. A soccer ball is kicked with initial speed u0 at an angle α above the horizon￾tal. Neglecting air resistance, what is the ball’s speed at its maximum height?
A. u0.
At the top, the vertical component has dropped to zero, so the speed is less than the launch
speed unless α = 0.
B. u0 cos α.
At maximum height the vertical velocity is zero while the horizontal component remains u0 cos α,
so the speed equals that value.
C. u0 sin α.
This is the initial vertical component, which becomes zero at the highest point.
D. 0.
Only the vertical component becomes zero at the peak; the horizontal component generally
remains nonzero.

Q11. A constant force F⃗ = (−2.50 N) ˆı + (6.00 N) ˆȷ acts on a particle as it moves
along the y axis from y = −1.0 m to y = 3.0 m. What is the work done by the
force on the particle?
A. 24 J.
The displacement is ∆⃗r = 4.0 ˆȷ so W = F⃗ · ∆⃗r = (6.00)(4.0) = 24 J and the x-component does
no work.
B. −10 J.
This comes from incorrectly using only the x-component of force even though the motion is
purely along y.
C. 14 J.
This kind of value typically results from mixing components or using the wrong displacement
magnitude.
D. 0 J.
Work is not zero because the force has a nonzero component along the displacement direction
(the y-direction).
